title: Hastings 1895
summary: A young American in his first big tournament, Harry Nelson Pillsbury, wins one of the strongest events ever held. Here he beats Tarrasch.

steps.title: Hastings, 1895
steps.text: In 1895 the English seaside town of Hastings hosted a tournament with almost every great player of the day: the world champion Emanuel Lasker, the former champion Wilhelm Steinitz, Siegbert Tarrasch and Mikhail Chigorin among them. The winner was a 22-year-old American few of them knew, Harry Nelson Pillsbury, in his first big international tournament. This is his game against Tarrasch, one of the favourites.
steps.narration: Hastings, 1895. Nearly every great player in the world is there, and the winner is a young American almost nobody knew: Harry Nelson Pillsbury. Here he plays Siegbert Tarrasch.

steps.title: Pillsbury – Tarrasch, Hastings 1895
steps.text: This game is a race. Tarrasch pushes his pawns on the queenside and wins material there. Pillsbury puts a knight on e5, pushes his f-pawn and aims everything at the black king. The game stops at Pillsbury's key moves.
steps.narration: Tarrasch attacks on the queenside, Pillsbury on the kingside. Who gets there first? Find Pillsbury's key moves.

notes.text: 11...c4: Tarrasch gains space on the queenside. His plan is to push the pawns on that side.
13.Ne5: a knight lands in the center.
14.f4: the f-pawn supports the knight. Pillsbury's plan is the opposite of Tarrasch's: attack the king.
21.f5: more space on the kingside, and Black's pieces get cramped.
27...b4: Tarrasch's queenside pawns are rolling. The race is on.
31...c3: Black's pawns are close to breaking through.
35.g4: Pillsbury's pawns finally move against the black king.
38...Bxb3: Tarrasch breaks through on the queenside and wins material.
40.gxf6: the g-file opens toward the black king.
45.Kh1: a quiet king move. The king leaves the g-file so a rook can use it.
52.Qxh7#: checkmate, with Black's c-pawn just one step from queening.

guesses.prompt: Black's ...f6 chases your knight from e5. Where should it go to stay near the black king?
guesses.hint: Head toward the kingside, close to f6 and h6.
guesses.why: 20.Ng4! The knight stays near the black king and eyes f6 and h6. Pillsbury keeps his pieces on the side where he is attacking.

guesses.prompt: Tarrasch has won material on the queenside. Pillsbury needs a strike on the kingside. Find the knight move.
guesses.hint: Your knight can jump to a square next to the black king and cover g8.
guesses.why: 42.Nh6! The knight covers g8, so Rg8 would now be mate. Tarrasch had to block with 42...Rg7, and after the rooks came off his king was dragged into the open.

guesses.prompt: The black king has come out to h6. Bring your last piece into the hunt.
guesses.hint: The g-file is open, and your rook on f1 can use it.
guesses.why: 46.Rg1! The rook takes the g-file, and the king has even fewer squares. Tarrasch grabbed the f5 pawn, but the queen checks that follow win his queen.

guesses.prompt: You have won the queen for a rook, but Black's c-pawn is close to queening. Find the check that settles it.
guesses.hint: Check from d6, and look at what else the queen attacks there.
guesses.why: 50.Qd6+! The king goes to h5, the queen takes the knight on d7, and mate on h7 comes before the c-pawn can queen.

steps.title: The king is the target
steps.text: Tarrasch won the race on the queenside, but Pillsbury's pieces were all around the black king. When both sides attack on opposite wings, measure how close each attack is to a king, not to a pawn. Pillsbury won Hastings ahead of Chigorin, Lasker, Tarrasch and Steinitz.
steps.narration: Tarrasch won pawns. Pillsbury won the king. And the young American won the whole tournament, ahead of the world champion.

steps.title: The race
steps.question: Pillsbury and Tarrasch attacked on opposite wings. Why did Pillsbury's attack win?

options.text: It was aimed at the king, so it decided the game even though Tarrasch won material
options.why: Right. A mate ends the game, and an extra pawn does not.
They often work. Tarrasch's pawns did break through. They were just a step too slow.

options.text: Pillsbury was ahead in material all game
options.why: Pillsbury was behind in material for a long time. His attack was worth more.

steps.narration: One question about the race: why did Pillsbury win it?
